title: Dynamic helimagnetism via charged spin current
abstract: We present a theoretical and numerical study of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons that carry both charge and spin currents, deriving the effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian. Applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain, these equations yield two current-driven helical phases: a static helix stabilized by a pure spin current alone, and a coherently precessing helix that appears once a small charge-current component is added. For a given helical wavenumber, the precession angular frequency $ω$ and the canting ratio $Δ$ toward the hard axis follow analytically from the equations of motion, while the wavenumber $q_{\rm helix}$ of the precessing helix is selected by a heuristically constructed effective Lagrangian. Direct numerical integration of the same equations of motion reproduces all three observables wherever it yields a coherent helix. The helix chirality is set by a long-range, current-generated Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM)-type coupling rather than an intrinsic DM interaction, so materials without bulk or interfacial DM interactions could also host current-controlled helical order. Because the helical pitch, precession frequency, and canting ratio are all continuously tunable by the current amplitudes, these helices could serve as probes of spin currents.
summary: This theoretical work models how localized magnetic spins behave when coupled to conduction electrons carrying both charge and spin currents. It derives equations of motion showing that current flow can stabilize two types of helical magnetic order: a static type and a dynamic, precessing type. The findings demonstrate that these magnetic properties are continuously tunable by controlling the current amplitudes.
main_problem: The study investigates dynamic helimagnetism stabilized and controlled by the interplay of both charge and pure spin currents in localized spins coupled to conduction electrons.
main_result: The model predicts two distinct current-driven helical phases: a static helix from pure spin current, and a coherently precessing helix when a small charge-current component is added.
method: The authors derive effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian using the Closed-Time-Path Green's Function formalism, followed by analytical and numerical solutions.
model_or_system: The system consists of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons via an s-d exchange Hamiltonian, applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain.
key_observables: Precession angular frequency (ω), canting ratio (Δ), and helical wavenumber (q_helix).
important_parameters: Current amplitudes (charge and spin), which continuously tune the helical pitch, frequency, and canting ratio.
main_assumptions: The model assumes point-like exchange coupling and neglects shape anisotropy and dipolar coupling of the magnets.
figures_summary: Not specified by the notes, but the paper involves analytical determination and numerical testing of the derived equations of motion.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure detailing the model derivation (using CTPGF), approximations, deriving effective equations of motion (including spin torques and current-induced DM terms), and concluding with analytical and numerical testing of the predictions.
why_interesting: The explicit derivation of spin dynamics from current-coupled localized spins, using advanced quantum field techniques like CTPGF, provides a rich theoretical framework for understanding current-controlled magnetic textures relevant to open quantum systems.
